key_insight: PI-RADS-compliant prostate MRI can be performed at 0.55T with clinically acceptable image quality and lesion detection.
clinical_relevance: Low-field prostate MRI may expand access to diagnostic imaging while maintaining patient-level lesion detection comparable to 3T.
method: 15 healthy volunteers and 22 suspected prostate cancer patients underwent bi-parametric prostate MRI at 0.55T.
Protocol included tri-planar T2-weighted imaging and axial diffusion-weighted imaging aligned with PI-RADS.
Deep learning reconstruction was used to improve image quality and optimize low-field acquisition parameters.
evidence_signal: Using 3T as the reference, low-field MRI achieved acceptable diagnostic quality in 95% of patients and patient-level lesion detection sensitivity of 91% for both readers.
watch_item: This was a small single-study evaluation, so broader validation is needed before routine adoption across sites and scanner platforms.
paper_title: Feasibility of PI-RADS Compliant Prostate MRI at 0.55T
